_meta.purpose: Companion to the NIST SSDF starter pack: the failure modes the SSDF practices exist to prevent. frameworkTag 'SSDF', category 'Secure Development'.
_meta.origin: Moved verbatim from the inline `ssdfRiskTemplates` array in prisma/seed.ts (2026-11-08), so production receives it: prisma/seed.ts is never run on a deploy.
_meta.deliveredBy: scripts/seed-risk-templates.ts on every container start (scripts/entrypoint.sh), and prisma/seed.ts in dev, both through prisma/risk-template-fixtures.ts.

templates.title: Vulnerable Dependency Shipped
templates.description: A third-party component with a known vulnerability is included in a release because it was not caught by software composition analysis.

templates.title: Unreviewed Code Merged to Production
templates.description: Code reaches production without mandatory peer review, allowing defects or malicious changes to slip through.

templates.title: Secrets Committed to Source Control
templates.description: Credentials, tokens, or keys are committed to a repository and exposed to anyone with read access or in history.

templates.title: Exploitable Vulnerability Released
templates.description: A security defect reaches production because SAST/DAST and security testing were not performed or not gated in CI.

templates.title: Compromised Build Pipeline
templates.description: An attacker gains control of the CI/CD pipeline or build environment and injects malicious code into artifacts.

templates.title: Tampered or Unsigned Release Artifact
templates.description: A release artifact is altered after build, or ships without integrity verification information, so acquirers cannot detect tampering.

templates.title: Unpatched Disclosed Vulnerability
templates.description: A publicly disclosed vulnerability in the software is not remediated within its SLA because there is no coordinated vulnerability-disclosure and response process.
